recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. Future terminology changes should continue to rely on publication validation for HL7-defined codes, while preserving the existing code primitive allowance for single internal spaces because external and local code systems may use them.
issue_request: FHIR-5573 asked to remove spaces from value set codes defined by FHIR/HL7 where feasible, while recognizing that externally defined systems such as UCUM may legitimately have spaces in code values. Jira records the issue as Published/Persuasive and applied for DSTU1.
initial_application: Historical git-svn commit e995abe5d075934abc6de37f9449f057bcfbb82e (#5573 / svn r4059) changed internally defined codes such as "entered in error", "in progress", "on hold", "not in", and "nil known" to hyphenated forms across the then-current source. The Jira comments also state that publication tooling was updated so HL7 does not define codes with spaces.
additional_context: The current code primitive still allows single internal spaces, so FHIR-5573 is not a universal ban on every code value containing whitespace. Later FHIR-18441 and a 2020 Zulip thread discuss code datatype whitespace and XML canonicalization, but they do not reverse the narrower policy for HL7-defined terminology codes. Current source includes active CodeSystem and ValueSet build surfaces, and the current scan found no whitespace-containing concept codes in HL7/FHIR-owned systems.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current in-scope core terminology source has no HL7/FHIR-defined concept code with whitespace requiring correction for this issue.

related_jiras.note: Published clarification about code datatype whitespace and XML canonicalization; it helps prevent over-reading FHIR-5573 as a universal ban on all code whitespace.
